<!-- README.md -->

# Meower2 API

Meower2 is a revival of the Meower chat server. This repository documents its HTTP REST API, the CloudLink realtime websocket protocol, the group-chat roles & permissions system, bot accounts, and the companion uploads service — everything you need to build a client or a bot.

The documentation is generated from the server source code. Every endpoint, field, error type, status code and event name was taken directly from the implementation.

## Quick start

Log in and grab a token (all examples use a placeholder base URL — see [Base URLs](docs/getting-started.md#base-urls)):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username": "me", "password": "hunter2hunter2"}'
```

```json
{"error": false, "account": {…}, "token": "<session-token>"}
```

Read the latest home posts:

```bash
curl https://api.example.com/home/ -H "Token: <session-token>"
```

Post to home:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/home/ \
  -H "Token: <session-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"content": "Hello, Meower!"}'
```

Get realtime updates by connecting to CloudLink and authenticating with the same token — see [docs/cloudlink.md](docs/cloudlink.md).

<!-- docs/getting-started.md -->

# Getting started

## Base URLs

Base URLs depend on the instance you are talking to. For a local development
setup the defaults are:

| Service | Local default |
|---|---|
| REST API | `http://127.0.0.1:3001` |
| CloudLink (websocket) | `ws://127.0.0.1:3000/?v=1` |
| Uploads | `http://127.0.0.1:3002` |

All examples in this documentation use `https://api.example.com` for the REST
API and `https://uploads.example.com` for uploads — substitute your instance's
URLs.

**API prefix:** the v0 blueprint is mounted at both `/` and `/v0`, so
`POST /auth/login` and `POST /v0/auth/login` are the same endpoint. The docs
show the unprefixed paths; add `/v0` if your client expects it.

## Authentication

After logging in ([POST /auth/login](rest/auth.md#post-authlogin)) or
registering you receive a `token`. Send it on every authenticated request with
the **`Token` header**:

```
Token: <token>
```

- Logging in with an existing token as the `password` also works (the client
  uses this to resume sessions and for CloudLink `authpswd`).
- Deleting your account, revoking tokens (`DELETE /me/tokens`), or regenerating
  a bot token invalidates tokens.
- If the account has TOTP authenticators, login returns `401` with
  `{"error": true, "type": "mfaRequired", "mfa_methods": ["totp"]}`. Resend the
  request including `totp_code` (6 digits) or `mfa_recovery_code` (10 hex
  chars) in the body — or simply append the code to the end of `password` (see
  [auth.md](rest/auth.md#post-authlogin)).
- Bots authenticate the same way with their bot token and can never log in
  with a password (see [bots.md](bots.md)).

## Requests

- JSON bodies, `Content-Type: application/json`.
- Validation errors return `400 {"error": true, "type": "badRequest"}`.
- The websocket API uses JSON packets; see [cloudlink.md](cloudlink.md).

## Response conventions

- Successful responses are JSON and usually include `"error": false`.
- Errors are `{"error": true, "type": "<type>"}` plus an HTTP status code.
  Some errors carry extra fields (e.g. `mfaRequired` → `mfa_methods`,
  `chatBanned` → `expires`, `passwordRecentlyChanged` → `changed_at`).

Common error types returned by the framework:

| Status | `type` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `badRequest` | malformed JSON / schema validation failed |
| 401 | `Unauthorized` | missing or invalid `Token` |
| 403 | `missingPermissions` | generic forbidden |
| 404 | `notFound` | resource does not exist (also used to hide private resources) |
| 405 | `methodNotAllowed` | |
| 429 | `tooManyRequests` | ratelimit bucket exhausted |
| 500 | `Internal` | |
| 503 | `repairModeEnabled` | instance is in repair mode |
| 403 | `ipBlocked` | requester's IP is netblocked |
| 403 | `accountBanned` | banned account, or banned from a specific feature (restrictions) |

## Pagination

List endpoints take `?page=<n>` (1-based, 25 items per page) and return:

```json
{"error": false, "autoget": [ … ], "page#": 1, "pages": 4}
```

- `autoget` — the items.
- `page#` — the page returned (note the `#` in the key name).
- `pages` — total pages.

## IDs & timestamps

- **Posts** are ULIDs: 26-char Crockford base32 strings that sort by creation
  time (e.g. `01J8Z4K0A0BCDEFGHJKMNPQRST`).
- **Chats, invites, authenticators, reports, data exports** are UUID4 strings.
- **Files** (avatars, icons, attachments, emotes) are 24-char
  `[a-zA-Z0-9]` IDs served by the uploads service.
- **Usernames** match `[a-zA-Z0-9-_]{1,20}` and are unique case-insensitively.
- **Timestamps** are Unix seconds (`t.e`, `created`, `last_active`,
  `updated_at`, …).

## Ratelimits

Endpoints enforce per-bucket fixed-window limits; when a bucket is exhausted
the endpoint returns `429 {"error": true, "type": "tooManyRequests"}`. Buckets
are namespaced internally as `rtl:<bucket>:<subject>` — the main ones you'll
hit:

| Bucket | Limit |
|---|---|
| `post:<user>` | 6 posts/edits/deletes per 5s (bypassed by the `POST_RATELIMIT_BYPASS` flag) |
| `typing:<user>` | 6 per 5s |
| `update_chat:<user>` | 5 per 5s (chat updates, members, roles, emotes; invites use 10 per 5s) |
| `create_chat:<user>` | 5 per 30s |
| `config:<user>` | 10 per 5s |
| `react:<user>` | 5 per 5s |
| `relationships:<user>` | 10 per 15s |
| `report:<user>` | 3 per 5s |
| `login:i:<ip>` | 50 per 900s; `login:u:<user>` 5 failed attempts per 60s |
| `register:<ip>:s` | 5 per 900s (plus fail bucket) |
| `bots:create:<user>` | 5 per 60s |

## Root endpoints

### `GET /`

Instance info:

```json
{"captcha": {"enabled": false, "sitekey": "…or null"}}
```

### `GET /status`

Always available, even in repair mode or for blocked IPs:

```json
{
  "scratchDeprecated": true,
  "registrationEnabled": true,
  "isRepairMode": false,
  "ipBlocked": false,
  "ipRegistrationBlocked": false
}
```

### `GET /statistics`

```json
{"error": false, "users": 123, "posts": 4567, "chats": 89}
```

### `GET /ulist?page=n`

Currently online usernames, 25 per page (same pagination shape, `autoget`
contains public account objects).

## Account object

Public account objects (from `/users/<name>`, search, ulist, etc.) contain:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `_id` | string | username |
| `uuid` | string | account UUID |
| `flags` | int | [UserFlags](#userflags) bitfield |
| `permissions` | int | admin permission bitfield |
| `created` | int | unix seconds |
| `pfp_data` | int | built-in avatar id |
| `avatar` | string | uploaded icon file id or `""` |
| `avatar_color` | string | 6-char hex |
| `quote` | string | status/bio (max 360) |
| `display_name` | string | optional display name (≤32, `""` when unset) |
| `last_seen` | int | unix seconds |
| `bot` | bool | bot account flag |
| `bot_owner` | string | only on bot accounts — owner username |
| `lvl` | int | always `0` (legacy) |
| `banned` | bool | |

`GET /me` returns the same plus `ban` and all user settings
(`unread_inbox`, `theme`, `mode`, `layout`, `sfx`, `bgm`, `bgm_song`, `debug`,
`hide_blocked_users`, `hide_presence`, `profile_theme`, `active_dms`,
`favorited_chats`).

### UserFlags

| Bit | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `SYSTEM` | system account (Server, Notification, Announcement) |
| 2 | `DELETED` | deleted account |
| 4 | `PROTECTED` | protected account |
| 8 | `POST_RATELIMIT_BYPASS` | skips the post ratelimit |
| 16 | `ULTRA_HD_UPLOADS` | joke flag |
| 32 | `BOT` | bot account |

### Ban states & restrictions

`account.ban.state` is one of `none`, `temp_restriction`, `perm_restriction`,
`temp_ban`, `perm_ban`, with `expires` and `reason`. A `perm_ban` or unexpired
`temp_ban` blocks all authenticated requests (`403 accountBanned`).

Restriction bits on `ban.restrictions` block specific features (also returned
as `403 accountBanned`):

| Bit | Restriction |
|---|---|
| 1 | home posts |
| 2 | chat posts |
| 4 | creating chats / adding members |
| 8 | editing chat details |
| 16 | editing own profile (profile fields silently dropped) |

---

<!-- docs/rest/auth.md -->

# Authentication — `/auth`

Shared request body (`AuthRequest`) for both endpoints:

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `username` | string | yes | 1–20 chars |
| `password` | string | yes | 1–255 chars (8–72 enforced on register) |
| `totp_code` | string | no | exactly 6 digits |
| `mfa_recovery_code` | string | no | exactly 10 chars |
| `captcha` | string | no | ≤2000 chars (hCaptcha response) |

## `POST /auth/login`

No auth required. Ratelimits: `login:i:<ip>` 50/900s; `login:u:<user>` 5/60s on
failure.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username": "me", "password": "hunter2hunter2"}'
```

Response `200`:

```json
{"error": false, "account": { …account incl. config… }, "token": "…"}
```

Credential notes:

- `password` may be an **existing session token** instead of the real password
  (used for session resume and CloudLink `authpswd`). Bot accounts can **only**
  authenticate this way — they have no password.
- If the account has TOTP authenticators and no `totp_code`/
  `mfa_recovery_code` is given, the server tries appending the code to the end
  of `password` itself: last 6 chars → TOTP, last 10 chars → recovery code.
- Using a valid `mfa_recovery_code` **deletes all authenticators**, rotates the
  recovery code and sends an inbox alert.
- A password changed within the last 14 days is accepted but rejected with a
  hint (see errors).

### Errors

| Status | `type` | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | `Unauthorized` | bad credentials |
| 401 | `accountDeleted` | account is deleted |
| 401 | `mfaRequired` | 2FA needed; response includes `mfa_methods: ["totp"]` |
| 401 | `passwordRecentlyChanged` | old password still in the 14-day grace window; response includes `changed_at` |
| 401 | `Unauthorized` | wrong `totp_code`/`mfa_recovery_code` |
| 429 | `tooManyRequests` | |

## `POST /auth/register`

No auth required. `username` must match `[a-zA-Z0-9-_]{1,20}` (400 otherwise),
`password` must be 8–72 chars (400 otherwise). If the instance sets a captcha
secret, `captcha` is verified against hCaptcha.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/auth/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username": "newuser", "password": "hunter2hunter2"}'
```

Response `200`: same shape as login (`{error: false, account, token}`) — you
are logged in immediately.

### Errors

| Status | `type` | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `registrationDisabled` | instance closed registration |
| 403 | `registrationBlocked` | requester's IP is registration-netblocked |
| 403 | `invalidCaptcha` | |
| 409 | `usernameExists` | |
| 400 | `badRequest` | bad username format or password length |
| 429 | `tooManyRequests` | |

<!-- docs/rest/me.md -->

# Current user — `/me`

All endpoints require `Token` auth. Sensitive account-management endpoints
return `403 {"error": true, "type": "botsCannotDoThis"}` for bot accounts
(noted per endpoint).

## `GET /me`

Your full account incl. config (see [Account object](../getting-started.md#account-object)).

```bash
curl https://api.example.com/me -H "Token: $TOKEN"
```

`200 {"error": false, …account + settings…}`

## `DELETE /me`

Schedules the account for deletion in 7 days, revokes all tokens and
disconnects CloudLink sessions. Logging back in within 7 days cancels
(`delete_after` cleared). 🚫 bots.

| Body | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `password` | string | yes |

Errors: 401 `invalidCredentials` (wrong password), 403 `botsCannotDoThis`,
429, 403 `accountBanned`.

## `PATCH /me/config`

Update profile fields and settings. Unknown/absent fields are ignored;
`null` values are dropped. Ratelimit `config:<user>` 10/5s.

| Body | Type | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `pfp_data` | int | built-in avatar id |
| `avatar` | string | uploads file id, `""` to clear |
| `avatar_color` | string | 6-char hex (no `#`) |
| `quote` | string | ≤360 |
| `display_name` | string \| null | trimmed, ≤32, no control chars/newlines; `""`/`null` clears → `invalidDisplayName` 400 |
| `unread_inbox` | bool | |
| `theme` | string | ≤256 |
| `mode` | bool | light/dark |
| `layout` | string | ≤256 |
| `sfx` | bool | |
| `bgm` | bool | |
| `bgm_song` | int | |
| `debug` | bool | |
| `hide_blocked_users` | bool | |
| `hide_presence` | bool | also toggles ulist visibility |
| `profile_theme` | bool | |
| `favorited_chats` | string[] | capped at 50 |

Setting `avatar` claims the file with the uploads service (`unableToClaimAvatar`
500 on failure) and unclaims the old one. If you're restricted from
`EDITING_PROFILE`, profile fields are silently dropped.

Events: `update_config` to your sessions; `update_profile` to everyone when
`pfp_data`/`avatar`/`avatar_color`/`quote`/`display_name` change.

`200 {"error": false}`

## `GET /me/relationships`

```json
{"error": false, "autoget": [{"username": "…", "state": 1, "updated_at": 0}], "page#": 1, "pages": 1}
```

Relationship states: `0` none · `1` friend request sent (friends if mutual) ·
`2` blocking.

## `GET /me/friends`

```json
{"error": false, "friends": ["mutual"], "incoming": ["they sent a request"], "outgoing": ["I sent a request"]}
```

## `PATCH /me/password`

🚫 bots.

| Body | Type | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `old` | string | required |
| `new` | string | 8–72 chars |

The previous hash is kept for 14 days (login with it returns
`passwordRecentlyChanged`). Sends an inbox alert.

`200 {"error": false}` · Errors: 401 `invalidCredentials`, 403
`botsCannotDoThis`, 429.

## `GET /me/authenticators`

```json
{"error": false, "autoget": [{"_id": "uuid", "type": "totp", "nickname": "…", "registered_at": 0}], "page#": 1, "pages": 1}
```

## `POST /me/authenticators`

Register a TOTP authenticator. 🚫 bots.

| Body | Type | Required | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `password` | string | yes | |
| `type` | `"totp"` | yes | only `totp` |
| `nickname` | string | no | ≤32 |
| `totp_secret` | string | yes | 32 chars (from `GET /me/authenticators/totp-secret`) |
| `totp_code` | string | yes | 6 digits, verified against the secret |

`200 {"error": false, "authenticator": {_id,type,nickname,registered_at},
"mfa_recovery_code": "…"}`. Sends an inbox alert. Errors: 401
`invalidTOTPCode`, 401 `invalidCredentials`, 403 `botsCannotDoThis`, 400, 429.

## `GET /me/authenticators/totp-secret`

Generates a new secret + provisioning URI + QR SVG. 🚫 bots.

`200 {"error": false, "secret": "BASE32…", "provisioning_uri": "otpauth://…",
"qr_code_svg": "<svg…>"}`

## `PATCH /me/authenticators/<id>`

🚫 bots. Body `{nickname?: string ≤32}` → `200 {"error": false, …authenticator…}`.

## `DELETE /me/authenticators/<id>`

🚫 bots. Body `{password}` → `200 {"error": false}` + inbox alert.
Errors: 401 `invalidCredentials`, 404, 403 `botsCannotDoThis`, 429.

## `POST /me/reset-mfa-recovery-code`

🚫 bots. Body `{password}` → `200 {"error": false,
"mfa_recovery_code": "…"}` + inbox alert. Errors: 401 `invalidCredentials`,
429.

## `DELETE /me/tokens`

Revokes **all** your tokens and kicks every CloudLink session.
`200 {"error": false}`.

## `GET /me/reports?page=n`

Reports **you** filed, newest first. `autoget` entries contain the report doc
with your `reason`/`comment`/`time` merged in and `content` populated (post
stub `{_id,u,isDeleted}` or account object for user reports).

## `GET /me/export`

Current data-export request, if any exists (pending, or completed <7 days
old). `200`:

```json
{"_id": "uuid", "user": "…", "status": "pending|completed|failed", "created_at": 0, "completed_at": 0, "size": 12345, "expires_at": 0}
```

`size`/`expires_at` only when completed. 404 if none. 🚫 bots.

## `POST /me/export`

Request a new export (built in the background as a ZIP: `account.json`,
`settings.json`, `posts.json`, `post_revisions.json`, `chats.json`,
`relationships.json`, `reactions.json`, `reports_filed.json`, …). 429 if a
current request already exists. `200` returns the export doc. 🚫 bots.

## `GET /me/export/download`

Downloads the latest completed export (`meower-data-<username>.zip`), or 404.
🚫 bots.

## Change username

`POST /me/username` (auth required, not available to bots)

Renames the account. Every existing token keeps working; live CloudLink
connections for the account are closed so they reconnect under the new name.

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `username` | string | yes | 1-20 characters: letters, numbers, `-` and `_` |
| `password` | string | yes | the account's current password |
| `totp_code` | string | if 2FA is enabled | 6-digit authenticator code |

Rules:

- One change every 72 hours (`429 usernameChangeCooldown`, with `retry_after` in seconds).
- The old name is reserved for 30 days. During that time only the account that held it can take it back
  (`409 usernameReserved` for everyone else). Registering it is refused (`409 usernameExists`).
- `GET /users/<old name>` follows the account for the reservation period: the response is the account's
  profile with `renamed_from` set to the name that was requested.
- An inbox message (category `security`) is sent after a change.

Errors: `invalidCredentials` (401), `mfaRequired` (403), `invalidTOTPCode` (401), `illegalCharacters` (400),
`sameUsername` (400), `usernameExists` (409), `usernameReserved` (409), `usernameChangeCooldown` (429),
`botsCannotDoThis` (403).

```bash
curl -X POST "$API/me/username" -H "Token: $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username": "NewName", "password": "hunter2hunter2"}'
```

---

<!-- docs/rest/home.md -->

# Home — `/home`

The public timeline. Post objects are described in
[posts.md](posts.md#post-object).

## `GET /home/?page=n`

Paginated home posts, newest first. **Public** — anonymous callers always get
page 1.

```bash
curl https://api.example.com/home/
```

```json
{"error": false, "autoget": […posts…], "page#": 1, "pages": 12}
```

## `POST /home/`

Create a post on home. Auth required; `POST_RATELIMIT_BYPASS` accounts skip the
`post:<user>` 6/5s bucket.

| Body | Type | Required | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | string | no | ≤4000 |
| `nonce` | string | no | ≤64, echoed back in the `post` event |
| `attachments` | string[] | no | file ids, ≤10, **images and videos only** |
| `reply_to` | string[] | no | post ids in `home`, ≤10 |
| `stickers` | string[] | no | sticker ids, ≤10 (unknown ids dropped) |

Needs `content`, ≥1 attachment, or ≥1 sticker (400 otherwise). Restricted
accounts (`HOME_POSTS`) get `403 accountBanned`.

`200` — the created post object (with `"error": false`).

Errors: 400 `tooManyAttachments` / `tooManyReplies` / `tooManyStickers`, 400
`mediaOnly` when an attachment's file record isn't an image or video (SVG excluded),
500 `unableToClaimAttachment`, 401, 403, 429.

## `POST /home/typing`

Broadcasts a `typing` event for `home` (`{chat_id: "home", username}`) to all
clients. Ratelimit `typing:<user>` 6/5s.

`200 {"error": false}`

<!-- docs/rest/posts.md -->

# Posts — `/posts`

## Post object

```json
{
  "_id": "01J8Z4K0A0BCDEFGHJKMNPQRST",
  "post_id": "01J8Z4K0A0BCDEFGHJKMNPQRST",
  "post_origin": "home",
  "type": 1,
  "u": "author",
  "author": {"_id": "author", "uuid": "…", "flags": 0, "pfp_data": 1, "avatar": "", "avatar_color": "000000"},
  "t": {"e": 1700000000},
  "p": "post content",
  "attachments": [{"id": "fileid24…", "mime": "image/webp", "size": 1234, "filename": "x.png", "width": 10, "height": 10, "thumbnail_mime": "image/webp", "thumbnail_size": 500}],
  "reply_to": [ …embedded parent post objects… ],
  "reactions": [{"emoji": "👍", "count": 3, "user_reacted": false,
                 "users": ["alice", "bob", "carol"]}],
  "emojis": [{"_id": "fileid24…", "name": "party", "animated": false}],
  "stickers": [{"_id": "fileid24…", "name": "meowy", "animated": false}],
  "pinned": false,
  "isDeleted": false,
  "edited_at": 1700000100,
  "error": false
}
```

- `post_origin` — `"home"`, `"inbox"`, `"livechat"`, or a chat id. `type` is
  `2` for inbox posts, `1` otherwise.
- `reply_to` in responses is a list of embedded post objects (`null` entries
  when replies are stripped); when *creating* a post you send post **ids**.
- `emojis` is populated from `<:FILEID>` tokens found in the content —
  see [custom emoji](#custom-emoji-in-content).
- `nonce` is present on the `post` event if you sent one.

### Custom emoji in content

A chat emoji is embedded in content as `<:FILE_ID>`, e.g.
`<:aB3fG7hJkLmN0pQrStUvWx>`. Render it from the uploads service:
`GET {uploads}/emojis/<file-id>`.

## `GET /posts/?id=<post_id>`

Single post. 404 if it doesn't exist, is deleted, or you can't see its origin
(inbox posts that aren't yours, chats you aren't in). For **group chats**,
non-members (and anonymous callers) can still read the post when the chat's
`allow_sharing` is on **and** they pass a valid share token as `?s=<token>`
(see [`GET /posts/<id>/share`](#get-postspost_idshare)) — banned users count
as non-members.

## `GET /posts/<post_id>/context?limit=n`

The post plus up to `limit` (1–10, default 5) surrounding posts in the same
origin: `{post, before, after}`. For group chats, non-members additionally
need `share_context` on (implies `allow_sharing`) **and** a valid `?s=`
share token for that exact post — you can't crawl a chat by following edge
posts, since each post needs its own token.

## `GET /posts/<post_id>/share`

Auth required. Returns a signed share token (HMAC of the post id) that
grants non-members read access to that post via `?s=` on `GET /posts?id=`
and `GET /posts/<id>/context`. Ratelimit `share:<user>` 30/60s.

- `post_origin: "home"` → `{error: false, token: null}` (public already).
- Group chat: requester must be a member (non-member → 404) with
  `share_posts` → else 403 `missingPermission`.
- DM: members → 403 `sharingUnavailable`; non-members → 404.

```json
{"error": false, "token": "a1b2c3…(32 hex chars)"}
```

## `PATCH /posts/?id=<post_id>`

Edit **your own** post (body: `PostBody`, only `content` is applied; must be
non-empty). In group chats the author needs the `edit_messages` permission
(403 `missingPermission`). Restricted users (`HOME_POSTS`/`CHAT_POSTS` per
origin) → 403 `accountBanned`. Editing the first message of a pending DM request → 403
`dmRequestPending`. Creates a revision entry, sets `edited_at`, emits
`update_post`.

## `DELETE /posts/?id=<post_id>`

- Own post in `home` or a DM: always allowed.
- Group chats: own post needs `delete_own_messages`; someone else's needs
  `delete_others_messages` **and** `outranks(actor, author)`; `Server` posts
  need rank ≥ 4 (admin tier). See [chat-permissions](../chat-permissions.md).
- Group chats with `announce_deletes` get a `Server` message announcing the
  deletion (`announce_deleter` controls whether the deleter is named).

`200 {"error": false}` · Errors: 403 `missingPermission`,
`insufficientRank`, 403/404/429.

## `DELETE /posts/<post_id>/attachments/<attachment_id>`

Remove an attachment from your own post; deletes the post entirely if no
content/attachments remain. 404 if the attachment isn't on the post.

## `POST /posts/<post_id>/report`

Body `{reason?: string ≤2000, comment?: string ≤2000}`. Three reports from
unique IPs auto-escalate and hide the post. Ratelimit `report:<user>` 3/5s.
`200 {"error": false}`.

## `POST /posts/<post_id>/pin` · `DELETE /posts/<post_id>/pin`

Pin/unpin a post in its origin chat. Group chats: `pin_messages` /
`unpin_messages` permission (site moderators with `EDIT_CHATS` bypass). Emits
`update_post` and a `Server` announcement message. Returns the post.
Errors: 403 `missingPermission`, 401/404.

## `GET /posts/<chat_id>?page=n`

Posts in a chat you belong to (group or DM), newest first. Auth + membership.

## `POST /posts/<chat_id>`

Post in a chat. Body = `PostBody` (same fields/constraints as
[home](home.md#post-home)) — attachments must be images or videos or the request fails
with 400 `mediaOnly`. Chat id `livechat` is special: the post is
broadcast to everyone but never stored.

- Group chat → needs `send_messages` permission (403 `missingPermission`).
- Chat-banned → 403 `chatBanned` + `expires`.
- **DM requests**: between non-friends, whoever posts first becomes the
  requester — the first message must be **text only** (`dmRequestTextOnly`),
  then the requester is blocked until the recipient replies or accepts
  (`dmRequestPending`). The recipient replying accepts the request.
- Blocked in either direction → 403 (bare `missingPermissions`).

`200` — created post. Emits `post` to chat members (everyone for
`livechat`), `update_chat` when a DM request changes.

`reactions[].users` is up to 3 usernames who reacted with that emoji, most
recent first (the requester is always first if they reacted).

## `GET /posts/<post_id>/reactions/<emoji>?page=n`

Users who reacted with `<emoji>` (unicode emoji or chat-emoji file id).
`autoget` = account objects.

## `POST /posts/<post_id>/reactions/<emoji>`

React. `<emoji>` must be exactly one unicode emoji or an existing chat-emoji
file id. Max 50 distinct reactions per post → 403 `tooManyReactions`. Group
chats need `react` when joining a reaction already on the post, or
`add_reactions` when the emoji isn't on the post yet → 403
`missingPermission`. Removing your own reaction is always allowed.
Ratelimit 5/5s.

`200 {"error": false}` + `post_reaction_add` event
`{chat_id, post_id, emoji, username}`.

## `DELETE /posts/<post_id>/reactions/<emoji>/<username>`

Remove a reaction; `<username>` may be `@me` for yourself. Removing **another
user's** reaction is only allowed for the chat owner (and only in chats).
404 if the reaction doesn't exist. `200 {"error": false}` +
`post_reaction_remove` event (same shape).

---

<!-- docs/rest/users.md -->

# Users — `/users/<username>`

`username` is case-insensitive; responses always use canonical casing. Deleted
or unknown users → 404 on every route in this blueprint.

## `GET /users/<username>/`

Public profile — no auth required. See
[Account object](../getting-started.md#account-object); includes `bot` and
`bot_owner` for bot accounts. `display_name` is the user's optional display
name (`""` when unset); embedded post `author` objects include it too.

```bash
curl https://api.example.com/users/JoshAtticus/
```

## `GET /users/<username>/posts?page=n`

The user's home posts, newest first. Public.

## `GET /users/<username>/relationship`

Your relationship **to** that user. Auth required; 400 if `<username>` is you.

```json
{"state": 0, "updated_at": 1700000000}
```

States: `0` none · `1` friend request (friends if mutual) · `2` blocking.

## `PATCH /users/<username>/relationship`

Change your relationship. Ratelimit `relationships:<user>` 10/15s.

| Body | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `state` | `0 \| 1 \| 2` | yes |
| `notify` | bool | no — only meaningful with `state: 2` |

`200 {state, updated_at}`

Side effects:

- `state: 1` — sends a friend-request inbox message; if the target already sent
  you a request you become friends (inbox messages to both, pending DM
  requests between you auto-accepted). Emits `update_friends`.
- `state: 0` — removes your relationship and clears their pending request to
  you; unblocking restarts the DM-request expiry countdown and clears a block
  notice they had set.
- `state: 2` — removes any friend request/friendship from them. With
  `notify: true`, the target gets your DM pushed to the front of their active
  DMs with `block_notice: <you>` so they can see they were blocked.
- Always emits `update_relationship` `{username, state, updated_at}` to your
  sessions.

## `POST /users/<username>/report`

Body `{reason?: string ≤2000, comment?: string ≤2000}`. Ratelimit 3/5s.
`200 {"error": false}`.

## `GET /users/<username>/dm`

Get or create your DM chat with the user. Auth; ratelimit
`create_chat:<user>` 5/30s; 400 if it's yourself.

- Returns the existing DM if there is one.
- If you aren't friends and the chat isn't already in your `active_dms`, the
  DM gets a pending `dm_request` slot (`{from: null, to: null,
first_message_sent: false}`): whoever posts first becomes the requester — see
[posts](posts.md#post-postschat_id) and [chats](chats.md#dm-requests).
- Non-friends creating a DM requires the `NEW_CHATS` restriction to be off
  (403 `accountBanned`).

`200` — the chat object with `emojis`/`stickers`/`error`.

---

<!-- docs/rest/chats.md -->

# Chats — `/chats`

All endpoints require `Token` auth unless noted. Most chat-management routes
share the `update_chat:<user>` ratelimit bucket (5 per 5s; 10 per 5s for
invites). Roles & permissions are covered in
[chat-permissions.md](../chat-permissions.md).

## Chat object

```json
{
  "_id": "uuid",
  "type": 0,
  "nickname": "my group",
  "icon": "",
  "icon_color": "000000",
  "owner": "username",
  "members": ["…"],
  "created": 0, "last_active": 0,
  "deleted": false,
  "announce_deletes": false, "announce_deleter": false,
  "roles": [ …role objects… ],
  "member_roles": {"user": ["default", "administrator"]},
  "invites_enabled": true,
  "allow_sharing": true,
  "share_context": false,
  "bans": [{"username": "…", "banned_by": "…", "banned_at": 0, "expires": null}],
  "emojis": [{"_id": "file-id", "name": "…", "animated": false}],
  "stickers": [{…}],
  "error": false
}
```

- `type`: `0` group chat · `1` DM.
- `allow_sharing`/`share_context` (groups only; `allow_sharing` defaults to `true`, `share_context` to `false` except in Announcements chats): whether
  non-members may read this chat's posts via `GET /posts?id=` and
  `/posts/<id>/context`; they additionally need a per-post share token
  (`?s=`, see [`GET /posts/<id>/share`](posts.md#get-postspost_idshare)),
  and context requires `share_context`.
- `dm_request` (DMs only) appears when a request is pending:
  `{from, to, first_message_sent}` — `ignored`/`created` are never exposed.
- `block_notice` (DMs only) is the username of the member who blocked the
  other with `notify: true`.
- Role object: `{_id, name, tier (−1–4; −1 = cosmetic), permissions: {perm: bool},
display_override?: bool, preset: bool, colors?: string[]}`.

## `GET /chats/`

All your chats: every group you belong to plus your `active_dms` and
favorited DMs. `{error, autoget, page#:1, pages:1}`.

## `POST /chats/`

Create a group chat. Ratelimit `create_chat:<user>` 5/30s; 150-group cap →
403 `tooManyChats`; `NEW_CHATS` restriction → 403 `accountBanned`.

| Body | Type | Required | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nickname` | string | yes | 1–32 |
| `icon` | string | no | uploads file id (claimed; 500 `unableToClaimIcon`) |
| `icon_color` | string | no | 6-char hex |
| `purpose` | string | no | `friends` `public` `private` `announcements` `emojis` `other` — tweaks preset roles/invites (see [purposes](../chat-permissions.md#chat-purposes)) |
| `announce_deletes`/`announce_deleter`/`invites_enabled` | bool | no | also accepted |

The creator becomes `owner` with `["default", "administrator"]` roles.
`200` — chat object + `create_chat` event to you.

## `GET /chats/<chat_id>`

Your member view of one chat (legacy groups are migrated to roles on read).
404 if not a member.

## `PATCH /chats/<chat_id>`

Update fields — each field you actually change is checked individually (all
permitted or nothing applies):

| Field | Permission (groups) |
|---|---|
| `nickname` | `change_name` |
| `icon` non-empty | `change_icon` |
| `icon: ""` | `delete_icon` |
| `icon_color` | `change_color` |
| `announce_deletes`, `announce_deleter` | `change_settings` |
| `invites_enabled` | `toggle_invites` |
| `allow_sharing`, `share_context` | `change_settings` |

`share_context` can only be `true` while `allow_sharing` is `true`:
turning `allow_sharing` off forces `share_context` off; setting
`share_context: true` while sharing is off → `400 sharingDisabled`.

DMs: only the owner may patch. `EDITING_CHAT_DETAILS` restriction → 403.
Emits `update_chat` and `Server` announcement posts. `200` — chat object.
Errors: 403 `missingPermission`, 500 `unableToClaimIcon`.

## `DELETE /chats/<chat_id>`

- **Group**: leave. Ownership passes to `members[0]` (new owner gains
  `administrator`); last member out deletes the chat and its posts.
- **DM**: removes it from your `active_dms` only.

Emits `delete_chat` to you. `200 {"error": false}`.

## `POST /chats/<chat_id>/typing`

Broadcast `typing` `{chat_id, username}` to members (`livechat` works too).
`200 {"error": false}`.

## `PUT /chats/<chat_id>/members/<username>`

Legacy "add member". Groups need `invite_members`; with `invites_enabled`
off, only the owner or `toggle_invites` holders may add (403
`invitesDisabled`). If the target **is a friend** they're added directly;
otherwise a [chat invite](invites.md) is sent instead (invite object
returned). New members get the `default` role. Errors: 403 `chatFull` (256
members), `chatBanned`, 409 `chatMemberAlreadyExists`, 403 if either party
blocks the other, 404.

## `DELETE /chats/<chat_id>/members/<username>`

Remove a member — `remove_members` + `outranks(actor, target)`. Errors: 403
`missingPermission` / `insufficientRank`, 404.

## `POST /chats/<chat_id>/members/<username>/transfer`

Owner only. New owner gains `administrator`. `200` — chat.

## `POST /chats/<chat_id>/invites`

Body `{username: 1–20, expires_in?: 60–2592000 (seconds)}` → creates a pending
invite: `{_id, chat_id, from, to, created, expires, error:false}`. Same
permission gate as adding members (`invite_members`, `invitesDisabled`).
409 `inviteAlreadyExists` if one is pending. The invitee gets a `chat_invite`
event + inbox message; members get `chat_invites_update`.

## `GET /chats/<chat_id>/invites`

Pending invites for the chat (expired ones are swept first).
`{error, autoget:[{_id,chat_id,from,to,created,expires}], page#:1, pages:1}`.

## `POST /chats/<chat_id>/dm_request/accept` · `POST /chats/<chat_id>/dm_request/ignore`

DM requests (recipient only — the `dm_request.to` user). Accept clears the
request and posts a `Server` notice; ignore flags it and removes the DM from
your `active_dms` (nothing is sent to the requester). 403/404 otherwise.

## `PUT /chats/<chat_id>/bans/<username>`

`ban_members` + `outranks(actor, target)` (never the owner). Body
`{expires_in?: 60–2592000}` (`null` = permanent). Removes the member and any
invites to/from them. `200 {"error": false, "ban": {username, banned_by,
banned_at, expires}}`.

## `GET /chats/<chat_id>/bans`

Active bans (unexpired); `ban_members` only.

## `DELETE /chats/<chat_id>/bans/<username>`

Unban; `ban_members` (+ outranks if still a member).

## `GET /chats/<chat_id>/pins?page=n`

Pinned posts in the chat (any member).

## Emotes — `/chats/<chat_id>/emojis|stickers`

- `GET /chats/<chat_id>/<emojis|stickers>` — list `{_id,name,animated}`.
- `GET /chats/<chat_id>/<emojis|stickers>/<id>` — one emote.
- `PUT /chats/<chat_id>/<emojis|stickers>/<id>` — create; `<id>` is an uploads
  file id, body `{name}` (1–32, `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`). `add_emotes` (DMs free).
  Caps: 250 emojis / 50 stickers → `tooManyEmojis`/`tooManyStickers`; 400
  `nameRequired`, 409 `nameTaken`, 500 `unableToClaimEmote`. Emits
  `create_emoji`/`create_sticker`.
- `PATCH …` — rename; `edit_emotes`. Emits `update_emoji`/`update_sticker`
  `{_id, chat_id, name}`.
- `DELETE …` — `delete_emotes`; unclaims the file. Emits
  `delete_emoji`/`delete_sticker` `{_id, chat_id}`.

## Roles — `/chats/<chat_id>/roles`

Group chats only. Rules in [chat-permissions](../chat-permissions.md#role-api).

- `POST /chats/<chat_id>/roles` — body `{name: 1–32, tier: −1–3,
permissions: {perm: bool}, display_override?: bool, colors?: string[0–2]
(6-hex)}`. Needs `create_roles`; non-owner/admin actors need `tier < rank(actor)`;
each `true` perm needs `PERMISSIONS[perm] ≤ tier` and grant rights. Tier −1
(cosmetic) roles store `permissions: {}` regardless of what you send, and
are the only roles that may have `display_override` (else 400
`notCosmetic`). Errors: 400 `unknownPermission` / `permissionAboveRoleTier`
/ `badColors` / `notCosmetic`, 403 `missingPermission` / `insufficientRank`.
`200` — role object.
- `PATCH /chats/<chat_id>/roles/<role_id>` — `{name?, tier?, permissions?:
{perm: true|false|null}, display_override?, colors?}` (`null` = reset to
inherit). `modify_roles` + `can_manage_role`; the `administrator` role only
  accepts a `colors` change from the owner, and its tier is locked (400
  `tierLocked`). Tier changes need `new_tier < rank(actor)` for non-owners;
  see [tier changes](../chat-permissions.md#changing-a-roles-tier) for the
  permission/override resets. `display_override` requires tier −1 (400
  `notCosmetic`).
- `DELETE /chats/<chat_id>/roles/<role_id>` — `delete_roles` +
  `can_manage_role`; `default`/`administrator` can't be deleted (403).
- `PUT /chats/<chat_id>/members/<u>/roles/<role_id>` /
  `DELETE …` — assign/unassign. `assign_roles` + `outranks(actor, target)` +
  `can_manage_role`; actors can't change their own roles (owner excepted);
  `administrator` can only be (un)assigned by the owner and never removed
  from the owner.
- Every change emits `update_chat` `{_id, roles, member_roles,
invites_enabled?}`.

---

<!-- docs/rest/invites.md -->

# Chat invites — `/invites`

Auth required. Invites are created via
[`POST /chats/<id>/invites`](chats.md#post-chatschat_idinvites) (or the legacy
`PUT …/members/<u>` when the target isn't a friend).

Invite object:

```json
{"_id": "uuid", "chat_id": "uuid", "chat_nickname": "…", "chat_owner": "…",
 "from": "inviter", "to": "you", "created": 0, "expires": null}
```

`expires` is a unix timestamp or `null` (never). Expired invites are deleted
lazily and treated as 404.

## `GET /invites/`

Your pending invites: `{error, autoget, page#:1, pages:1}`.

## `POST /invites/<invite_id>/accept`

Join the chat — `default` role assigned. Emits `create_chat` to you,
`update_chat` to members, `chat_invites_update`, and a `Server` join message.
`200` — the chat object.

Errors: 404 (unknown/expired invite or deleted chat), 403 `chatFull` (256
members), 403 `chatBanned` + `expires`.

## `DELETE /invites/<invite_id>`

Decline an invite addressed to you, or revoke one. Revoking is allowed for
the invitee, the inviter, or any member with `remove_members`. Emits
`chat_invites_update`. `200 {"error": false}` · Errors: 403/404.

---

<!-- docs/rest/inbox.md -->

# Inbox — `/inbox`

Auth required. The inbox is a private post feed: messages addressed to you
plus `Server` announcements (friend requests, invites, security alerts,
announce-deletes notices are *not* here — those are chat posts).

## `GET /inbox/?page=n&category=<cat>`

Posts where `u` is you or `Server` in origin `inbox`, newest first, 25/page.

Optional `category` filters by the post's inbox category — one of
`friends`, `chats`, `security`, `moderation`, `announcement`, `account`
(anything else → 400). Pagination applies after the filter.

```json
{"error": false, "autoget": […post objects (type 2)…], "page#": 1, "pages": 3}
```

Each inbox post object carries `category` — one of the above, or `null`
when the message wasn't categorised (clients show a generic
"Notification" label).

New inbox posts arrive over CloudLink as `inbox_message` events, and a
Server-originated inbox post flips your `unread_inbox` flag.

---

<!-- docs/rest/search.md -->

# Search — `/search`

Both endpoints are **public** (no auth needed). Query params:

| Param | Type | Required | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `q` | string | yes | 1–4000 chars (MongoDB text search) |
| `page` | int | no | ≥1, default 1 |

## `GET /search/home?q=…&page=n`

Full-text search over non-deleted home posts → post page shape.

## `GET /search/users?q=…&page=n`

Full-text search over usernames/quotes → `autoget` of account objects.

> Note: the underlying query requires `pswd` to be a string, so bot accounts
> (and any other passwordless accounts) never appear in user search.

---

<!-- docs/rest/emojis.md -->

# Default emoji packs — `/emojis`

## `GET /emojis/<lang>`

The server's built-in emoji set, localized. `lang` is one of:
`ar de en es fa fr id it ja ko pt ru tr zh` (404 otherwise).

```json
{"error": false, "groups": [
  {"slug": "people", "name": "People", "icon_emoji": "😀",
   "emojis": [
     [["😀", "😀"], [":grinning_face:", ":smiley:"]],
     …
   ]}
]}
```

Each emoji entry is `[[unicode variants…], [":name:", ":aliases:"]]`.

This is the static picker data — chat-scoped custom emojis/stickers live
under [`/chats/<id>/emojis` and `/chats/<id>/stickers`](chats.md#emotes---chatschat_idemojisstickers)
and are embedded in posts as `<:file-id>` (see
[posts.md](posts.md#custom-emoji-in-content)).

---

<!-- docs/rest/bots.md -->

# Bot management — `/bots`

Bots are real accounts (`flags` has bit `32`/`BOT`, `pswd` is `null`) that
authenticate everywhere with a single bot **token** — never a password.
See the [bots guide](../bots.md) for usage.

Management endpoints need a normal (non-bot) `Token`; bots get
`403 {"error": true, "type": "botsCannotManageBots"}` on every route except
the public `GET /bots/<id>`. Destructive actions (delete, token regenerate)
require a `totp_code` when the **owner** has TOTP authenticators:
`403 mfaRequired` if absent, `401 invalidTOTPCode` if wrong.

## `POST /bots/`

Create a bot. Ratelimit `bots:create:<user>` 5/60s; max 10 bots per owner.

| Body | Type | Required | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | must match `[a-zA-Z0-9-_]{1,20}` |
| `description` | string | no | ≤250, default `""` |

`200`:

```json
{"error": false, "id": "mybot", "name": "mybot", "description": "…",
 "owner": "you", "token": "…", "icon": ""}
```

`token` is returned **only here** (and on regenerate).

Errors: 400 `illegalCharacters`, 409 `usernameExists` (case-insensitive, vs
all accounts), 403 `botsCannotManageBots` / `tooManyBots`, 429.

## `GET /bots/?page=n`

Your bots, 25/page: `{error, bots: [{id, name, icon}], page, pages}`.

## `GET /bots/<id>`

**Public** — no auth needed:

```json
{"error": false, "id": "mybot", "name": "mybot", "description": "…", "owner": "you", "icon": ""}
```

404 `notFound` if it doesn't exist.

## `PATCH /bots/<id>`

Owner only. Body `{name?: string|null, description?: string|null}`.
`name` is immutable — any value that differs → `400 nameImmutable`.
`200` — same shape as GET.

## `DELETE /bots/<id>`

Owner only + MFA check (optional JSON body `{totp_code}`). Deletes the bot
account **and** its posts/relationships (the bot's token stops working).
`200 {"error": false}`.

## `POST /bots/<id>/token/regenerate`

Owner only + MFA check (optional `{totp_code}`). Replaces the bot's tokens
with one new token and kicks its CloudLink sessions.

`200 {"error": false, "token": "…"}`

## Notes

- Deleting the owner cascades: all their bots (metadata + accounts) are
  deleted too.
- A bot's public profile (`GET /users/<name>`) shows `bot: true` and
  `bot_owner`.

---

<!-- docs/rest/admin.md -->

# Admin — `/admin`

Requires `Token` auth plus a non-zero `permissions` bitfield on the account
(401 otherwise). Each route also checks a specific
[AdminPermissions](#adminpermissions-bitfield) bit — insufficient bits →
403 `missingPermissions`.

## AdminPermissions bitfield

| Bit | Name |
|---|---|
| 1 | `SYSADMIN` |
| 2 | `VIEW_REPORTS` |
| 4 | `EDIT_REPORTS` |
| 8 | `VIEW_NOTES` |
| 16 | `EDIT_NOTES` |
| 32 | `VIEW_POSTS` |
| 64 | `DELETE_POSTS` |
| 128 | `VIEW_ALTS` |
| 256 | `SEND_ALERTS` |
| 512 | `KICK_USERS` |
| 1024 | `CLEAR_PROFILE_DETAILS` |
| 2048 | `VIEW_BAN_STATES` |
| 4096 | `EDIT_BAN_STATES` |
| 8192 | `DELETE_USERS` |
| 16384 | `VIEW_IPS` |
| 32768 | `BLOCK_IPS` |
| 65536 | `VIEW_CHATS` |
| 131072 | `EDIT_CHATS` |
| 262144 | `SEND_ANNOUNCEMENTS` |

## Reports

| Route | Permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /admin/reports?status&type&page` | VIEW_REPORTS | `status`: `pending` `escalated` `no_action_taken` `action_taken`; `type`: `post`/`user` |
| `GET /admin/reports/<id>` | VIEW_REPORTS | |
| `PATCH /admin/reports/<id>` | EDIT_REPORTS | `{status: "no_action_taken"\|"action_taken"}` |
| `POST /admin/reports/<id>/escalate` | EDIT_REPORTS | |

## Admin notes

| Route | Permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /admin/notes/<identifier>` | VIEW_NOTES | `identifier` is a user UUID |
| `PUT /admin/notes/<identifier>` | EDIT_NOTES | `{notes}` |

## Posts

| Route | Permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /admin/posts/<post_id>` | VIEW_POSTS | incl. revisions & deleted |
| `DELETE /admin/posts/<post_id>` | DELETE_POSTS | `mod_deleted` |
| `POST /admin/posts/<post_id>/restore` | DELETE_POSTS | |

## Users

| Route | Permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /admin/users?page` | any user-moderation bit | |
| `GET /admin/users/<username>` | varies | fields gated per-permission (netlog VIEW_IPS, alts VIEW_ALTS, ban VIEW_BAN_STATES, full profile SYSADMIN) |
| `PATCH /admin/users/<username>` | SYSADMIN | `{permissions?: int}` |
| `DELETE /admin/users/<username>?mode=` | DELETE_USERS (SYSADMIN for non-own) | `mode`: `cancel` `schedule` `immediate` `purge` |
| `POST /admin/users/<username>/ban` | EDIT_BAN_STATES (SYSADMIN for others) | `{state: "none"\|"temp_restriction"\|"perm_restriction"\|"temp_ban"\|"perm_ban", restrictions: int, expires: int, reason: str}` |
| `GET /admin/users/<username>/posts?origin&page` | VIEW_POSTS / VIEW_CHATS | |
| `DELETE /admin/users/<username>/posts?origin=` | DELETE_POSTS (SYSADMIN for others) | |
| `POST /admin/users/<username>/alert` | SEND_ALERTS | `{content: 1–4000}` → inbox message |
| `POST /admin/users/<username>/kick` | KICK_USERS | disconnect CloudLink sessions |
| `POST /admin/users/<username>/restore-password` | SYSADMIN | |
| `DELETE /admin/users/<username>/avatar` | CLEAR_PROFILE_DETAILS | |
| `DELETE /admin/users/<username>/quote` | CLEAR_PROFILE_DETAILS | |

## Chats

| Route | Permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /admin/chats/<chat_id>` | VIEW_CHATS | |
| `PATCH /admin/chats/<chat_id>` | EDIT_CHATS | `{nickname?, icon?, icon_color?}` |
| `DELETE /admin/chats/<chat_id>` | EDIT_CHATS | marks `deleted` |
| `POST /admin/chats/<chat_id>/restore` | EDIT_CHATS | |
| `POST /admin/chats/<chat_id>/members/<username>/transfer` | EDIT_CHATS | |
| `GET /admin/chats/<chat_id>/posts?page` | VIEW_CHATS | |

## Network

| Route | Permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /admin/netinfo/<ip>` | VIEW_IPS | accounts seen from the IP |
| `GET /admin/netblocks?page` | VIEW_IPS | |
| `GET /admin/netblocks/<cidr>` | VIEW_IPS | |
| `PUT /admin/netblocks/<cidr>` | BLOCK_IPS | `{type: 0\|1}` — 0 blocks access, 1 blocks registration |

<!-- docs/cloudlink.md -->

# CloudLink realtime protocol

CloudLink is the websocket API for live events. Local default:
`ws://127.0.0.1:3000/?v=1`.

## Connecting & protocol version

- `?v=1` selects protocol **v1** (any other/missing value → legacy **v0**).
- `?token=<token>` auto-authenticates on connect (skips `authpswd`).
- All packets are JSON objects with at least `{"cmd": str, "val": any}`;
  `listener` is an optional client-chosen string echoed back on replies.

On connect the server sends a `ulist` packet (online users, `;`-separated,
trailing `;`). v0 clients additionally get a `statuscode` `TAEnabled`.

## Sending commands

Commands can be sent at the root — `{"cmd": "authpswd", "val": {…}}` — or
wrapped — `{"cmd": "direct", "val": {"cmd": "authpswd", "val": {…}}}`. A
direct wrapper whose `val` is a **string** marks the socket "trusted" and
returns `OK` (legacy handshaking).

| Client command | val | Response |
|---|---|---|
| `ping` | any | `statuscode: I:100 \| OK` |
| `get_ulist` | any | `ulist` packet |
| `authpswd` | `{username, pswd}` | `auth` packet + `statuscode OK` |
| `gen_account` | `{username, pswd, captcha?}` | `auth` packet + `statuscode OK` |

`authpswd` proxies `POST /auth/login` — `pswd` may be a password **or an
existing token** (that's how bots log in). Auth errors are mapped to
statuscodes (`Unauthorized`→`PasswordInvalid`, `mfaRequired`→`2FARequired`,
`usernameExists`→`IDExists`, `accountDeleted`→`Deleted`,
`accountBanned`→`Banned`, `tooManyRequests`→`RateLimit`,
`invalidCaptcha`→`InvalidCaptcha`, `passwordRecentlyChanged`→`statuscode`
`PasswordRecentlyChanged` with `changed_at`, `ipBlocked`/`registrationBlocked`→`Blocked`).

### `auth` packet (v1)

```json
{"cmd": "auth", "val": {
  "username": "…", "token": "…",
  "account": { …account + config… },
  "relationships": […],
  "chats": […]          // omitted for v0 clients
}}
```

## Events (v1)

Every event is `{"cmd": <name>, "val": <payload>}`:

| `cmd` | Payload | Audience |
|---|---|---|
| `ulist` | `"user1;user2;"` | everyone |
| `statuscode` | status string | requester |
| `auth` / `banned` | see above / `ban` object | requester |
| `post` | full post object | all (home/livechat) or chat members |
| `update_post` | full post object | same |
| `delete_post` | `{chat_id, post_id}` | same |
| `inbox_message` | post object (`type` 2) | recipient (or all when `u` is `Server`) |
| `typing` | `{chat_id, username}` | chat members (`home`/`livechat` → all) |
| `create_chat` | chat object | the user the chat appeared for |
| `update_chat` | `{_id, …changed fields…}` (e.g. `members`, `owner`, `roles`, `member_roles`, `invites_enabled`, `bans`, `dm_request`, `block_notice`, `nickname`, `icon`…) | chat members |
| `delete_chat` | `{chat_id}` | the affected user |
| `update_config` | changed config keys | all your sessions |
| `update_profile` | `{_id, pfp_data?/avatar?/avatar_color?/quote?}` | everyone |
| `update_relationship` | `{username, state, updated_at}` | your sessions |
| `update_friends` | `{}` | the two users |
| `chat_invite` | invite + `chat_nickname` | invitee |
| `chat_invites_update` | `{chat_id}` | chat members |
| `create_emoji` / `create_sticker` | `{_id, name, animated}` | chat members |
| `update_emoji` / `update_sticker` | `{_id, chat_id, name}` | chat members |
| `delete_emoji` / `delete_sticker` | `{_id, chat_id}` | chat members |
| `post_reaction_add` / `post_reaction_remove` | `{chat_id, post_id, emoji, username}` | post audience |

## Events (v0 translation)

For `v`≠1 clients the same events are wrapped differently:

- Root commands `statuscode`, `ulist`, `pmsg`, `pvar` → `{"cmd": <name>,
"val": …}`.
- Everything else → `{"cmd": "direct", "val": {"mode": <event>, "payload":
…}}`, except:
  - `post` on home → `{"cmd": "direct", "val": {"mode": 1, …post…}}`; other
    origins → `"state": 2` instead of `mode`.
  - `typing` home → `{"state": 101, "chatid": "livechat", "u": user}`; other
    → `{"state": 100, "chatid": <chat>, "u": user}`.
  - `delete_chat` / `delete_post` → `{"mode": "delete", "id": <id>}`.
  - `auth` includes no `chats` field.

## Statuscodes

`{"cmd": "statuscode", "val": "<code>"}` (with `listener` when replying to a
packet that had one):

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `I:100 \| OK` | success |
| `E:101 \| Syntax` | malformed packet |
| `E:102 \| Datatype` | wrong `val` type |
| `E:103 \| ID not found` | |
| `E:104 \| Internal` | server error in handler |
| `E:106 \| Too many requests` | REST ratelimit mapped |
| `I:112 \| Trusted Access enabled` | sent to v0 clients on connect |
| `E:116 \| Username required` | |
| `E:118 \| Invalid command` | |
| `E:119 \| IP Blocked` | |
| `I:011 \| Invalid Password` | login failed |
| `E:126 \| Password recently changed` | + `changed_at` |
| `E:127 \| Invalid captcha` | |
| `I:015 \| Account exists` | register conflict |
| `I:016 \| 2FA Required` | mfaRequired |
| `E:018 \| Account Banned` | |
| `E:025 \| Deleted` | account deleted |

<!-- docs/chat-permissions.md -->

# Group chat roles & permissions

Applies to **group chats only** (`type` 0). DMs have no roles — every member
can do everything a DM allows. The site-wide `EDIT_CHATS` admin permission
overrides pin/unpin and the admin endpoints.

## Chat fields

Group chats carry three extra fields:

- `roles` — list of role objects (see below).
- `member_roles` — `{username: [role_id, …]}`.
- `invites_enabled` — bool (default `true`).
- `allow_sharing` — bool (default `true`): non-members may read shared posts.
- `share_context` — bool (default `false`, `true` for Announcements chats; forced off while `allow_sharing`
  is off): non-members may also read surrounding context.

## Role object

```json
{"_id": "default", "name": "Default", "tier": 0,
 "permissions": {"send_messages": true}, "preset": true,
 "colors": ["ff8800"]}
```

- `_id` — preset roles have stable ids; custom roles use UUIDs.
- `tier` — integer −1–4 (see [tiers](#tiers)); changeable via PATCH except
  for `administrator`.
- `permissions` — `{perm_key: bool}`. `true` = Allow, `false` = Deny,
  key absent = Inherit.
- `colors` — up to 2 six-hex strings (none / solid / gradient); cosmetic.
- `preset` — built-in role.

## Permissions

| Key | Tier |
|---|---|
| `send_messages`, `delete_own_messages`, `invite_members`, `add_emotes`, `edit_emotes`, `delete_emotes`, `change_color`, `change_name`, `change_icon`, `delete_icon`, `pin_messages`, `unpin_messages`, `add_reactions`, `share_posts`, `react`, `edit_messages` | 0 |
| `delete_others_messages`, `remove_members` | 1 |
| `ban_members`, `modify_roles`, `assign_roles` | 2 |
| `change_settings`, `create_roles`, `delete_roles`, `toggle_invites` | 3 |

## Tiers

- Role tiers are −1–3 for creatable roles (**−1 = Cosmetic**: grants no
  permissions and is excluded from inheritance); **4 = Administrator** (all
  permissions, preset only); **owner rank = 5**.
- A permission can only be set to `true` on a role whose tier ≥ the
  permission's required tier.
- `rank(user)` = owner → 5; else max tier of their roles; no roles → −1.
- `outranks(a, b)` = `rank(a) > rank(b)` — required for removing, banning,
  deleting others' messages and assigning roles.
- Grant rule: a non-owner/non-admin actor can only grant a permission whose
  tier is **strictly below** their rank.

## Effective permissions (inheritance)

`role_effective(role)`:

1. Tier ≥ 4 → **all** permissions.
2. Tier −1 (cosmetic) → **no** permissions, ever.
3. Start with every permission any **lower-tier, non-cosmetic** role
   explicitly allows.
4. Add this role's own `true`s.
5. Remove this role's own `false`s.

Denies do **not** cascade upward: a `false` on a lower-tier role only
affects that role. `member_permissions(user)` = owner → all; non-member →
none; else union over their roles.

### Cosmetic roles & `display_override`

- A `tier: -1` role is cosmetic: `permissions` is always `{}` (permission
  edits are stripped server-side) and it contributes nothing to inheritance.
- Roles carry `display_override` (bool, default `false`), allowed **only**
  on cosmetic roles (setting it `true` on any other tier → 400
  `notCosmetic`; moving a role off tier −1 resets it to `false`).
- The role shown for a member (name + colour): if the member has any role
  with `display_override`, the **most recently assigned** of those wins;
  otherwise the highest-tier role (ties → most recent).

### Changing a role's tier

`PATCH /chats/<id>/roles/<rid>` accepts `tier` in −1..4:

- `administrator`'s tier can never change → 400 `tierLocked`.
- The actor must manage the role at its current tier **and** the new tier:
  the owner may set any tier, anyone else needs `new_tier < rank(actor)`
  (else 403 `missingPermission`).
- Effects: → −1 strips `permissions`; leaving −1 strips `permissions` and
  resets `display_override`; lowering a numeric tier drops explicit `true`
  allows for perms whose required tier is above the new tier (explicit
  `false` denies are kept).

## Preset roles

| id | Name | Tier | Grants |
|---|---|---|---|
| `default` | Default | 0 | send_messages, delete_own_messages, invite_members, add_reactions, share_posts, react, edit_messages |
| `stickerer` | Stickerer | 0 | add_emotes, edit_emotes, delete_emotes |
| `customiser` | Customiser | 0 | change_color, change_name, change_icon, delete_icon |
| `pinner` | Pinner | 0 | pin_messages, unpin_messages |
| `minimod` | Minimod | 1 | delete_others_messages, remove_members |
| `moderator` | Moderator | 2 | ban_members, modify_roles, assign_roles |
| `higher_moderator` | Higher Moderator | 3 | change_settings, create_roles, delete_roles, toggle_invites |
| `administrator` | Administrator | 4 | *(all)* |

New chats: owner gets `["default", "administrator"]`, everyone else
`["default"]`. Removing `default` is the mute mechanism — without it a
member can't send.

## Role API rules

Endpoints in [chats.md — roles](rest/chats.md#roles---chatschat_idroles).

- `can_manage_role(actor, role)` — never for `administrator` (except the
  owner changing its `colors`, and owner-only assignment); owner or rank ≥ 4
  → always; else `role.tier < rank(actor)`.
- Self role changes: non-owner actors cannot add/remove **their own** roles.
- `default` can be removed from a member (mutes them); `default` and
  `administrator` can't be deleted; `administrator` can't be edited and can
  never be removed from the owner.
- After any roles/`member_roles`/`invites_enabled` change the server sends
  `update_chat {_id, roles, member_roles, invites_enabled?}` to members.

## Chat purposes

`purpose` (creation-only field on `ChatBody`) adjusts the preset `default`
role and `invites_enabled`:

| Purpose | Effect |
|---|---|
| `friends` | default gains all stickerer + customiser + pinner permissions |
| `public` | presets unchanged |
| `private` | `invites_enabled: false`, `allow_sharing`/`share_context` false, Default role without `share_posts` (everything else as normal) |
| `announcements`, `emojis` | default reduced to `add_reactions` + `react` + `share_posts` + `edit_messages` |
| `other` / omitted | presets unchanged |

## Legacy migration

Group chats created before roles get migrated lazily (`ensure_roles`) and in
a startup pass: roles = presets, owner → `default`+`administrator`, other
members → `default` (plus `pinner` if they had `allow_pinning`),
`invites_enabled: true`, `allow_pinning` removed.

<!-- docs/bots.md -->

# Bots

Bots are real Meower accounts (username, profile, posts, DMs — everything)
that authenticate with a long-lived **bot token** instead of a password.
Each account can own up to **10** bots; owners can manage them in
**Settings → Account → Bots** or via [`/bots`](rest/bots.md).

## Creating a bot

**Settings UI**: Settings → Account → Bots → Manage → create with a name +
optional description. The token is shown **once** — copy it immediately.

**API**:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/bots/ \
  -H "Token: $YOUR_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "mybot", "description": "hello"}'
# → {"error": false, "id": "mybot", "name": "mybot", "token": "BOT_TOKEN", …}
```

Deleting a bot or regenerating its token prompts for a 6-digit TOTP code if
your account has one (API: `mfaRequired` / `invalidTOTPCode`).

## Using the token

REST — send it as the `Token` header, same as a user token:

```bash
curl https://api.example.com/me -H "Token: $BOT_TOKEN"
```

CloudLink — `authpswd` with the token as `pswd`
(`?token=…` query auth works too):

```json
{"cmd": "authpswd", "val": {"username": "mybot", "pswd": "BOT_TOKEN"}}
```

## Restrictions

- Password login → 401 (bots can't log in with a password, and no password
  exists).
- `pswd: null`, so bots never appear in user search results.
- `/bots` management endpoints → 403 `botsCannotManageBots`.
- Self-service `/me` routes (delete account, password change, authenticators,
  data export) → 403 `botsCannotDoThis`.
- Profiles show `"bot": true` and `"bot_owner": "<owner>"`; delete the owner
  and their bots go with it.

## Example bot (Node.js)

Node 22+ has a global `WebSocket` (on 18–21 `npm i ws` and
`import WebSocket from "ws"`).

```js
const API = "http://127.0.0.1:3001";      // REST base
const WS  = "ws://127.0.0.1:3000/?v=1";   // CloudLink
const BOT = "mybot";
const TOKEN = "BOT_TOKEN";

const ws = new WebSocket(WS);
ws.onopen = () => ws.send(JSON.stringify({
  cmd: "authpswd", val: { username: BOT, pswd: TOKEN },
}));
ws.onmessage = async (ev) => {
  const { cmd, val } = JSON.parse(ev.data);
  if (cmd === "post" && val.p === "!ping") {
    // home posts go to POST /home, chat posts to POST /posts/<chat id>
    const path = val.post_origin === "home" ? "/home" : `/posts/${val.post_origin}`;
    await fetch(`${API}${path}`, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Token": TOKEN, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ content: "pong" }),
    });
  }
};
```

## Example bot (Python)

`pip install requests websockets`

```python
import asyncio, json, requests, websockets

API, WS_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:3001", "ws://127.0.0.1:3000/?v=1"
BOT, TOKEN = "mybot", "BOT_TOKEN"

async def main():
    async with websockets.connect(WS_URL) as ws:
        await ws.send(json.dumps({
            "cmd": "authpswd",
            "val": {"username": BOT, "pswd": TOKEN}}))
        async for raw in ws:
            pkt = json.loads(raw)
            if pkt["cmd"] == "post" and pkt["val"]["p"] == "!ping":
                origin = pkt["val"]["post_origin"]
                path = "/home" if origin == "home" else f"/posts/{origin}"
                requests.post(
                    f"{API}{path}",
                    headers={"Token": TOKEN}, json={"content": "pong"})

asyncio.run(main())
```

<!-- docs/uploads.md -->

# Uploads service

The uploads service is a **separate Go service** (Chi router + MongoDB +
MinIO object storage + ImageMagick), not part of the Quart REST server.
Local default: `http://127.0.0.1:3002`.

> Note: this is documented from the uploads service source in the workspace
> (`uploads/router.go`, `uploads/file.go`, `uploads/user.go`) plus what the
> client calls.

## Buckets

| Bucket | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `icons` | user avatars & chat icons | |
| `emojis` | custom chat emojis | |
| `stickers` | chat stickers | |
| `attachments` | post attachments | images get `width`/`height`/`thumbnail_*` metadata |

## `POST /<bucket>`

Multipart upload (`multipart/form-data` with the file field). Auth:
`Authorization: <token>` (a `usersv0` token — same as the REST `Token`
header). The file id returned is then **referenced** in REST calls —
`attachments`/`stickers` arrays on posts, `icon` on chats, emote ids on
`/chats/<id>/emojis` — and the REST server "claims" it (500
`unableToClaim*` errors if the id doesn't exist in uploads).

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3002/icons \
  -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" -F "file=@avatar.png"
```

## `GET /<bucket>/<file_id>`

Download a file by its id. No auth required.

## `DELETE /<bucket>/<file_id>`

Delete a file you uploaded (`Authorization` header as above).
